answer_1.quote: We introduce DART, a large and open-domain structured Data-Record-to-Text generation corpus... Data-to-Text generation aims to produce natural language output from structured input.
answer_1.outputs: textual descriptions generated from structured data records (tables, triples)

answer_2.quote: We report BLEU, METEOR, and TER... we also report MoverScore, BERTScore, and BLEURT... we include PARENT which explicitly aligns n-grams from the reference and generated text to the data contents.

answer_4.quote: We ask 5 internal annotators to evaluate on 100 triplesets... Each tripleset is paired with 3 sentences... We defined three levels of fluency: fluent, mostly fluent, and not fluent, and the same for semantic faithfulness.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators evaluate each sentence on fluency (fluent, mostly fluent, not fluent) and semantic faithfulness (faithful, mostly faithful, not faithful).
